primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: X-linked nephrogenic diabetes insipidus due to AVPR2 loss of function
mechanism: AVPR2 encodes the basolateral vasopressin V2 receptor in collecting-duct principal cells. Normal V2-receptor activation stimulates Gs, adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, and PKA, leading to apical insertion of AQP2 water channels; AVPR2 loss of function disrupts this pathway and prevents urinary concentration.
vignette: A boy has lifelong polyuria, polydipsia, recurrent dehydration, and episodes of hypernatremia. Urine remains very dilute despite water deprivation and does not concentrate after desmopressin. Genetic testing identifies a loss-of-function variant in AVPR2.
lead: Which of the following intracellular responses is most directly impaired in the collecting duct?
correct: Gs-cAMP-PKA signaling that promotes apical insertion of aquaporin-2 water channels
distractors: Aldosterone-induced transcription of epithelial sodium-channel subunits
NKCC2-mediated sodium-potassium-chloride transport in the thick ascending limb
Urea recycling through inner-medullary collecting-duct transporters
Angiotensin-II-mediated constriction of the efferent arteriole
distractor_notes: Aldosterone regulates sodium transport through ENaC but is not the vasopressin V2-receptor pathway disrupted by AVPR2 loss.
NKCC2 operates in the thick ascending limb and contributes to medullary hypertonicity but is not the receptor-specific signaling defect in this patient.
Urea recycling contributes to the medullary osmotic gradient, but AVPR2 loss directly impairs the cAMP/PKA-dependent AQP2 insertion response.
Angiotensin II affects renal hemodynamics and sodium handling but is not the collecting-duct vasopressin signaling cascade.
key_expl: Vasopressin binds the V2 receptor on the basolateral membrane of collecting-duct cells and activates Gs, adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, and PKA. This signaling promotes insertion of AQP2 channels into the apical membrane. AVPR2 loss therefore prevents the normal antidiuretic response even when vasopressin or desmopressin is present.
objective: Explain X-linked nephrogenic diabetes insipidus as AVPR2 loss causing failure of Gs-cAMP-PKA-mediated apical AQP2 insertion.
